doc.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012

title: Goodbyes and other jazz filmmakers to interview
summary: They thank each other and Crohn suggests Don McGlynn and Joel Katz as further interviewees.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: All right. Well thank you, Burrill.
And it’s been nice having you for a friend and a colleague.

Yes, Monk, friend and colleague. I feel one of the great benefits of the Joe Williams film was we got to meet, and that’s another blessing, and will continue to be. And go get Don McGlynn and get — who else should you get — I’ll tell you. There are other people
making films about jazz. And right here we have Joel Katz who made the film about the lyrics to “Strange Fruit.”
He did that film? It was on PBS?

He’s local. And he may have done that interview, he’s friends with Jack DeJohnette. He may have done the interview with Jack DeJohnette that’s on the web site. Because I know he’s shot some footage of Jack DeJohnette in a recording session. I will pass on names of people. And by the way, they do things other than jazz but some of them have done things on jazz that are really worth seeing and talking about. And I’m glad you opened up this avenue in your archive.
Yeah, I’m glad that that guy —
